Kelby Town 3 Ashford Rovers 2

Kelby Town came from two goals down in the last twenty minutes to win the County Cup for the first time in 41 years, with substitute Callum Breen scoring the winner in the fourth minute of stoppage time at a packed Millbrook Park.

Ashford Rovers, who had beaten Kelby twice in the league this season, looked in control at half-time. Their captain Jonah Mensah headed in a corner after eleven minutes, and winger Ellis Haddad doubled the lead with a low shot from the edge of the area just before the break.

Kelby manager Ruth Adeyemi made two changes at the start of the second half and switched to three at the back. For a long spell nothing seemed to change. Rovers goalkeeper Sam Ortega was barely tested until the 71st minute, when Kelby's Dan Firth turned in a cross at the near post.

The equaliser came eight minutes later. Ashford failed to clear a long throw, and centre-back Ollie Whitmore volleyed in from twelve yards. The Kelby end, which had been quiet for most of the afternoon, did not sit down again.

With extra time looming, Breen, who had been on the pitch for less than ten minutes, collected a loose ball on the halfway line, ran at a tiring defence and curled his shot into the far corner. Ashford had one last chance from a free kick, but Mensah's header went over the bar.

"I told them at half-time that one goal changes everything," Adeyemi said afterwards. "They believed it. Most of these players grew up within a few miles of this ground, and they have given the town a day it will talk about for years."

Ashford manager Kofi Larbi was gracious in defeat. "For seventy minutes we were excellent. Then we stopped doing the simple things. That is football, and Kelby deserve their day," he said.

The win earns Kelby a place in next season's regional Challenge Trophy and prize money of twelve thousand pounds, which the club says will go towards new floodlights. The trophy will be paraded through the town centre on Saturday morning.
